questions.answer: School location and reputation as well as cultural experiences.

questions.answer: Better guidance about classes would have been great.

questions.answer: Was pretty easy. Good introduction meeting as well as info on teams/mail. Good helpdesk as well.

questions.answer: Tough. I can't recommend anything unfortunately.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got most of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in good time when registering.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic of level varied a lot. The workload was varying a lot from course to course. Would never take financial statement analysis due to very high workload relatively to other classes. When on exchange that is just crasy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More like highschool with smaller classes and student participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Operations strategy, Sports career seminars, Corporate social responsibility, financial crisis in history, strategy costing, energy finance, global energy markets, financial statement analysis.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Recommend Operations strategy because it is easy. Financial crisis in history is very interesting but teacher is a bit hard to understand.
